cells.tense: You can let an ending be finished and keep the feeling of it with you.
cells.act: let the feeling settle into its own depth
cells.ask: Give the thing that's ending ten quiet minutes. After those minutes: no fixing, no plan. The feeling sinks as far as it goes, unpushed.
cells.core:
The thinking goes all the way down here, and you come back with your feet under you. What's ending doesn't take the feeling with it, and you're not trying to make it.

Different endings want different things. Some want the company kept longer; others are done wanting it, and you'll feel the difference as you sit. Give the thing that's ending ten quiet minutes. After those minutes, no fixing, no plan, nothing to report. The feeling sinks as far as it goes, unpushed. By the next morning you can tell whether those minutes moved you toward the finish or stayed beside it. Both tell you something. The rest of the week stays yours.
cells.sheetLine: You can end it and keep what it left.
cells.verb: Going underneath the surface of your own thinking.
cells.place: At the clearing where something ends.

cells.tense: You'll keep digging underneath until the under-thing is finally safe, and there will be no bottom to reach.
cells.act: state the order of things once, without argument
cells.ask: Name the shape of one ending out loud in a sentence. Once. Then let it stand, undefended, for the rest of the day.
cells.core:
You keep going underneath, and the deeper you go the more certain you are that one more look will settle it. Your thinking has reached its own floor about this clearing. Something other than thought has to move it.

Breaking the surface means naming what you see. Name the shape of one ending out loud in a sentence — to yourself if you're alone, to one person if someone's there. Say it once, then let it stand undefended for the rest of the day. If the words are wrong, name new ones tomorrow. Today these hold. The urge to re-examine will come back by evening, and you can notice it and add nothing.
cells.sheetLine: The digging is a job now — name it once and stop.

cells.tense: The ending you were close to is years behind you, and you still haven't settled what you felt about it.
cells.act: mark the good thing together, out loud
cells.ask: With the people who were there at that ending — or one of them — say out loud the good the time held, small enough for one breath.
cells.core:
That ending is years back, and what you felt about it is still unfinished. You can go deep on anything — machinery, markets, the moves at work — but this particular clear belongs to a door you didn't decide to close, and you walk around that corner instead of through it.

With the people who were there at that ending — or one of them — say out loud the good the time held. Keep it small enough for one breath, and say it before anything else does. A little talk is plenty. Whether they've earned it doesn't need answering first. What you say out loud belongs to the room then, not only to you.

cells.tense: You're already handling the ending — keeping some, letting go of others — and calling it just getting through the week.
cells.act: stay with the quiet of it
cells.ask: Ten minutes with a piece of what you're carrying — a memory, a room, a habit. No task, no clock-watching. Just stay where you are with it.
cells.core:
You're already in the middle of the change, deciding what stays and what goes. You do it well, which is why it stays automatic — folded in with the day's logistics, no author, no banner. Just getting through this stretch.

The hand is yours. Ten minutes with a piece of what you're carrying — a memory, a room, a habit, a name. No task attached, nothing to decide, nothing to pack. Stay where you are with it. If a decision comes, fine. If the ten minutes change nothing, that's fine too. Next time this work comes up, those ten minutes beside it will be yours again, and this time you'll know it.
cells.sheetLine: The clearing already has an author — it has your hand.

attempts.check:
My unsupported claim is that a felt knowing is waiting under the thinking, since nothing in the record says what the person feels. To the deniable points: the Balanced cell would fail if the person is genuinely done wanting depth, yet a sitting still shows them what remains, at no cost; the Too Much cell would fail if the scrutiny no longer traps them, and the ask still works the first time it catches them; the Too Little cell would fail if the door is open, and noticing the gap still tells them where they stand; the Unacknowledged cell would fail if the hand were not theirs, and the pause still shows them whose it is (or isn't). The sentence that serves me more than them is the temptation to promise new light; I've traded it for what they can carry. 

Smaller fixes: I cut 'dip into,' 'widen the frame', and the light-through-water image rather than trim them; verified every ask is word-for-word one of the listed acts before writing it small; and made the four ask verbs open: give, break, share, take.
